text:
Elaine (CSM): Quick heads-up — AstraGrid called after today's demo. They're excited and want to expand beyond the pilot: add Support and Analytics teams for live call summarization + real-time alerting. They expect bursts up to ~3x our current trial qps and want an estimate for reserved capacity + pricing. Also flagged cost sensitivity for embeddings and a 300ms median token latency target.

Tom (Solutions): Awesome. Sounds like a Dedicated pilot makes sense. Recommend a small reserved pool first (4x A100-ish GPUs) and streaming endpoints for summarization. We should also offer a quantized model option to reduce cost.

Kiran (SE): +1. Can we propose a phased rollout: (1) Support team ingest (low concurrency), (2) Analytics team realtime (higher concurrency), (3) full routing with canary. I'll draft an enablement checklist. @Tom can you share the sample config?

Tom (Solutions): Pasting a minimal pilot config to validate capacity. We'll run this in staging before customer traffic:

```
model: redwood-llama-2-q4
pool_size: 4
max_concurrency_per_gpu: 12
batching: enabled
streaming: true
kv_cache: shared
autoscale: min:4,max:8,policy:latency
```

Tom (Solutions): That setup should handle sustained spikes and keep 95th pct latency under their 300ms target for short responses. We'll need to tune batch windows for short-turn summarization to avoid tail latency.

Sam (Eng): FYI from runtime side: we can enable prefix caching for repeated customer prompts (support templates) which will cut tokens and CPU. For analytics realtime we should use a smaller seq window and aggressive KV eviction. Also can enable local embedding cache for semantic lookup to reduce embedding calls.

Elaine (CSM): Great. Customer asked for a 30-day pilot price and an enterprise reserved quote (monthly). Can someone put together an estimate by EOD tomorrow? They want to present to procurement next week.

Kiran (SE): I can assemble the pilot cost model (GPU hours, token amortized, storage for KV cache). Tom/Sam — send any assumptions you want included by 2pm.

Sam (Eng): Sending assumptions now: average response length 60 tokens, call rate 200 rps peak per team (analytics), support 40 rps. Use q4 quantized model perf numbers.

Tom (Solutions): I'll run a small batch test tonight and paste results. If perf is good, recommend offering them a 10% discount on the first 3 months reserved to reduce renewal risk. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: load-test-schedule created — job id lt-20260321-01, starts 2026-03-22T02:00Z. Results will be uploaded to /mnt/tests/lt-20260321-01/report.json

Elaine (CSM): Action items: 1) Kiran to draft pilot + enterprise quote (due tomorrow EOD). 2) Tom to run perf test and share results (tonight). 3) Sam to provide caching/eviction assumptions (2pm). 4) I'll schedule a procurement prep call with AstraGrid for next Wednesday (invite incoming).

Kiran (SE): I'll also attach a short enablement deck and a one-pager with runbooks for on-call. Link: https://redwood.app/sales/astra-enablement (internal)

Elaine (CSM): Noted risk: they mentioned procurement will default to the cheapest option if we can't show cost savings vs their current vendor. Keep pricing defensible and highlight latency SLA and support SLAs.

Tom (Solutions): Agreed. We'll focus on e2e latency numbers from the load test and the cost per 1M tokens with quantized model.

Elaine (CSM): Thanks team — I'll sync after test results and the quote. Please react with :eyes: when you add your deliverables here so I can track.
